Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:10:1.hebrew: מה בעלים עד דמכוין ליה - ר' שמעון אית ליה הך סברא גבי רוצח באלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עט.), ורבנן פליגי עליה ואמרי: אף בעליו נמי, מתכוין להרוג את זה והרג את זה — חייב. דהאי ״וארב לו״, אמרי דבי רבי ינאי: רבנן מוקמי ליה פרט לזורק אבן לגו — לתוך חבורת אנשים ויש שם כנענים וישראלים, ואיכא למימר לכנענים נתכוין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:10:1.english: Just as [with] the owner, until he intends [to kill] him - Rabbi Shimon holds this reasoning regarding a murderer in [the chapter] Eilu Hen HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 79a), whereas the Rabbis disagree with him and say: even [regarding] the owner too, [one who] intends to kill this one and kills that one is liable. For this [phrase] "and lies in wait for him" [Deuteronomy 19:11], the school of Rabbi Yannai say [that] the Rabbis establish it [as] excluding one who throws a stone lego — [meaning] into a group of people where there are Canaanites and Israelites, and one can say he intended [to hit] the Canaanites.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:13:1.english: Derive [it] from the fact that the majority of them are Canaanites [gentiles] - And a verse is not needed to exempt him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:13:2.hebrew: ואי נמי - חמשה כנענים וחמשה ישראלים, לא איצטריך קרא למפטריה, דרחמנא אמר (במדבר ל״ה:כ״ה) "ושפטו העדה והצילו העדה", דהא ספק נפשות להקל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:13:2.english: Alternatively - [if there are] five Canaanites and five Jews, a verse is not needed to exempt him, for the Merciful One said (Numbers 35:25), "And the congregation shall judge, and the congregation shall rescue," since [in a case of] uncertainty [concerning] capital [law, the rule is] to [be] lenient.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:14:1.hebrew: לא צריכא דאיכא תשעה ישראלים - דאי לאו קרא, הוה אמינא זיל בתר רובא ולישראל איכוין. ואע"ג דדלמא לאו להאי איכוין — נתכוין להרוג את זה והרג את זה, חייב. קא משמע לן קרא, דהואיל והוה ליה כנעני קבוע ביניהן, כמחצה על מחצה דמי, וספק נפשות להקל. ולכל מילי דקיימא לן קבוע כמחצה על מחצה דמי, מהאי קרא נפקא לן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:14:1.english: It is only necessary where there are nine Jews - For if not for the verse, I would say: follow the majority, and he intended [to hit] a Jew. And even though perhaps he did not intend [to hit] this [particular person] — [the rule is that if] one intended to kill this [person] and killed that [person], he is liable. [Therefore,] the verse teaches us that since the Canaanite [i.e., gentile] is fixed among them, it is considered like half and half [i.e., equally balanced], and [in] a case of uncertainty [concerning] capital [law, the ruling is] to be lenient. And for all matters where we hold [that] something fixed is considered like half and half, it is derived from this verse.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:15:1.hebrew: שור היתומים - שאין להן אפוטרופוס, או שור אפוטרופוס — של יתומין, אלא שעל אפוטרופוס לשומרו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:15:1.english: An ox belonging to orphans - [This refers to orphans] who have no steward; or [in the case of] "an ox of a steward," [it also belongs] to orphans, except that it is upon the steward to guard it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:16:1.hebrew: שור שור ז' - ז' שור כתובין בפרשה בנוגח אדם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:16:1.english: “An ox,” “an ox,” seven [times] - Seven [times] “ox” [is] written in the [Torah] portion regarding [an ox] that gores a person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:16:2.english: An ox belonging to a woman - So that you should not say "the owner of the ox" is written in the masculine [gender].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:18:1.english: From [the fact] that it teaches two - an ownerless ox twice.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:18:2.hebrew: הא קמ"ל - הא דהדר תנא שור הגר לר' יהודה, דאע"ג דנגח בחיי הגר ומת והוי ליה הפקר, פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:18:2.english: It teaches us this - That which [the baraita] goes back and teaches "an ox of a convert" according to Rabbi Yehuda [is to teach] that even though it gored during the convert's lifetime and [he] died and it became ownerless, [it] is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:19:1.hebrew: והועד בבעליו - היינו בב"ד, דאין העדאה אלא בב"ד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:19:1.english: And warning has been given to its owner - That is, in court, for warning is only [given] in court.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:1:1.hebrew: ואכתי צרורות נינהו - ואין כופר כתוב אלא בנגיחה, דהוי גופו ממש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:1:1.english: But still, they are pebbles - And ransom is written only for goring, which is [with] its actual body.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:1:3.hebrew: מיניה מיניה - ע"י דחיפתו וגלגולו כל שעה עד שמפילו עליו, ומיהו אינו מתכוין להרוג:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:1:3.english: From it, from it - Through its pushing and rolling [the wall] continuously until it causes it to fall upon him; however, [the ox] does not intend to kill.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:22:1.hebrew: מסרו לשומר חנם - עד שלא נגח, ולאו ארישא קאי, אלא מילתא אחריתי היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:22:1.english: He handed it over to an unpaid bailee - [This is] before it gored, and it does not refer to the earlier clause; rather, it is a separate matter.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:22:2.english: In place of the owner - They become liable for damages like the owner.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:23:1.hebrew: אם עד שלא נגמר דינו מכרו מכור - ואפילו לרבנן, דלא דרשי בבעליו דנהוי מיתה והעמדה בדין כא', ומיחייב קטלא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:23:1.english: If before its verdict was issued he sold it, it is sold - And even according to the Rabbis, who do not expound b've'alav ("its owner") [to mean] that the killing and the standing for judgment must be as one, and [thus] it is liable to death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:2:1.hebrew: חייב בכופר ופטור מן המיתה - דדרשינן כופר אם כופר, והיינו כוותיה דשמואל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:2:1.english: Liable to [pay] ransom and exempt from death - For we expound "ransom," "if a ransom," and this is in accordance with Shmuel.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:4:1.english: And [for] the injuries - [where] an ox caused damage unintentionally and did not kill.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:5:1.english: From its ransom - For we say [that] he is liable [even] unintentionally, from the amplification [derived] from "if a ransom".

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:8:1.english: The liability of an ox - The payments for its damages come on account of the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:8:2.english: From the liability of an ox - [That is,] its being put to death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 44b:8:3.english: Ransom is the liability of the owner - [It is] an atonement for his soul.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:13:1.hebrew: הוה ליה פלגא ופלגא וספק נפשות להקל - תימה: למ"ד התראת ספק לא שמיה התראה, בלא טעמא דספק נפשות להקל פטרינן ליה מהאי טעמא דלא שמיה התראה, אפילו ס"ל דספיקא לחומרא. ואי אליבא דמ"ד שמיה התראה, היכי פטרינן ליה מהאי טעמא הכא אם נמצא שישראל הרג? הא מחייבינן ליה בהכה את זה וחזר והכה את זה אע"ג דספק הוא, ובנותר שאמר לו "אל תותיר"! וי"ל דשאני התם, דיודע בבירור דיבא לידי איסור ודאי אם יותיר או אם יכה את שניהם — משום הכי שמיה התראה; אבל הכא כשזורק אבן לגו, אין ידוע שיבא לידי איסור ודאי, שאין יודע את מי יכה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:13:1.english: It is half and half, and uncertainty [concerning] capital law is [treated] leniently - This is astonishing: According to the one who says that an uncertain warning is not considered a [valid] warning, [even] without the reason of "uncertainty [concerning] capital law is [treated] leniently," we would exempt him for this reason — that it is not considered a [valid] warning — even if one holds that an uncertainty is [treated] stringently. And if [the Gemara follows] the one who says that it is considered a [valid] warning, how do we exempt him for this reason here if it is found that he killed a Jew? Why, we hold him liable in [the case where] he struck this one and then struck that one, even though it is uncertain, and in [the case of] notar where [the witness] said to him, "Do not leave [any] over"! And one can answer that it is different there, because he knows with certainty that he will come to a definite prohibition if he leaves [any] over or if he strikes both of them — therefore it is considered a [valid] warning; but here, when he throws a stone into [a crowd], it is not known that he will come to a definite prohibition, for he does not know whom he will strike.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:14:1.hebrew: כל קבוע כמחצה על מחצה דמי - מהכא נפקא בכל דוכתי, כדאיתא בפ"ק דכתובות (דף טו.). ותימה: לר' שמעון קבוע מנא ליה? ואין לומר הכא כדמסיק בערכין (דף ז) ובהנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עט.): דר' שמעון יליף "נתינה נתינה", אייתר ליה "וארב לו" לקבוע — דאכתי לתנא דבי חזקיה קשה: מנא ליה דכל קבוע כו'? ועוד: כיון דפטר ר"ש אפילו בכולן ישראל עד שיאמר "לפלוני אני מכוין", לא שייך למדרשיה כלל. וי"ל: דלר' שמעון מיירי בכולן ישראל וכנעני אחד, ואמר "לאותו שעומד שם אני מכוין", דפטור מטעם קבוע מ"וארב לו", דכהאי גוונא כולן ישראל חייבין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:14:1.english: Any [item] fixed [in its place] is like half and half - [The rule of kavua] is derived from here in all places, as stated in the first chapter of Ketubot (15a). And it is astonishing: according to Rabbi Shimon, from where does he [derive the rule of] kavua? And one cannot say here as [the Gemara] concludes in Arakhin (7a) and in [the chapter] HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 79a) that [since] Rabbi Shimon derives [the exemption for unintended killing from] "giving, giving," "and he lay in wait for him" is left over [to teach] kavua — for still, according to the Tanna of the school of Chizkiyah, it is difficult: from where does he [derive] that any kavua [is like half and half], etc.? And furthermore, since Rabbi Shimon exempts [the killer] even when all of them are Jews unless he says, "I intend [to kill] so-and-so," it is not relevant to expound it [for kavua] at all! And one can answer that according to Rabbi Shimon, [the verse applies to a case] where all of them are Jews and one is a Canaanite [gentile], and he said, "I intend [to kill] that one who is standing there," where he is exempt on account of kavua from "and he lay in wait for him," for in such a case [if] all of them [were] Jews, he would be liable.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:16:1.english: "An ox," "an ox," seven [times], etc. - One [mention is] for itself, and six [are] to include [the six additional cases].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:16:2.hebrew: שור האשה - אצטריך לאתויי משום דאמר לעיל (בבא קמא מד ע"א): "כי יגח" — נגיחה למיתה, נגיחה לנזקין, ובנזקין כתיב "איש" דוקא; לכך אצטריך ריבוי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 44b:16:2.english: An ox belonging to a woman - It was necessary to include [this case] because [the Gemara] stated earlier (Bava Kamma 44a): "When [an ox] gores" — [one] goring for death, [and one] goring for damages, and regarding damages it is written "a man" specifically; therefore, an inclusion is necessary.
